sentences.text: The genus Neogaeornis is known only from a single tarsometatarsus, a fused foot bone, originally described by Lambrecht in 1929.
Despite the fragmentary nature of the fossil, evidence indicates that Neogaeornis was a diving bird.
Neogaeornis is classified as a controversial prehistoric genus of diving bird.
Recent phylogenetic studies suggest Neogaeornis is a basal loon, representing an early branch in the loon lineage.
A 2017 study placed Neogaeornis in the family Vegaviidae alongside Polarornis, Australornis, and Vegavis.
This animal lived approximately 70 to 67 million years ago.
Its fossil record spans the Maastrichtian stage, a geological period ranging from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Gerald Mayr argued that Neogaeornis may not belong to the family Vegaviidae because the specimen exhibits traits of other bird groups.
The taxonomic placement of Neogaeornis remains controversial due to uncertainty regarding its evolutionary relationships.
